notes: Measured in the browser on 2026-09-22 on main at 1c4992e8. Two lives won a seat in the state house on the same simulated day, February 2, 2026, one in Galena, Illinois and one in Lexington, Kentucky, both at 81 percent after twenty-seven door-knocking sessions.

Illinois seats the winner immediately. The office screen reads 'Dawn works for the Illinois legislature, so what is in front of the chamber is in front of them too', with a voting workflow, a casework policy and a bill docket.

Kentucky does not. The result reads 'Jasmine Carlson won. The supported term begins 2027-01-01; the result itself grants no current office authority.' Her office screen still reads 'You hold no office in this life yet. Running for one is under Campaigns when the game supports it here.' Ten weeks later it still reads that.

So one of the two is wrong and the game does not know which. Kentucky's eleven-month gap is the closer match to how American legislatures actually work; Illinois seating a winner the same afternoon is not. But an eleven-month gap in which the player holds nothing and the screen tells them they have never run for anything is not the right answer either.
This is separate from state-legislative-seat-calendar-and-field, which asks when the election is. This asks what happens between winning one and taking the seat.
The 2027-01-01 date Kentucky prints is itself worth checking against real law; it reads like a generic new-year default rather than a sourced commencement.
question: Between winning a state legislative election and being able to act as a legislator, what actually happens, and when? Specifically: how long is the gap between election day and the start of the term, state by state (a rule with exceptions named is enough); what, if anything, does a winner hold in that gap — is there a status such as member-elect, and what can a member-elect actually do; what marks the transition (a swearing-in, the chamber convening, a fixed calendar date); and how does a seat filled at a special election differ, since a special-election winner is usually seated at once?

sourcesChecked.source: Galena, Illinois and Lexington, Kentucky, walked in the browser to a win and ten weeks past it, main at 1c4992e8
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Establishes that the game does two contradictory things and that one of them leaves the player holding nothing with no explanation. It has no standing to say which is right.

sourcesChecked.source: The shipped legislature packs us-il-general-assembly-v1 and us-ky-general-assembly-v1
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Carry the chambers and who may stand. Neither was read for when a winner is seated, which is why the two states diverge.

sourcesChecked.source: The result sentence Kentucky prints, 'The supported term begins 2027-01-01'
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Shows the engine can already carry a term-start date and say so. Whether 2027-01-01 is Kentucky's real commencement, or a generic default, is not established anywhere this walk could read.

title: What a winner holds between election night and taking the seat
usableAnswer: The gap between election day and the start of a state legislative term, as a rule with its exceptions named rather than fifty entries; what a member-elect is and what they can do in that window (office setup, caucus votes for leadership, pre-filing bills — whatever is real); what event actually seats them; and how a special election differs. Approximate durations are fine. What is needed precisely is whether there is a real, named status in the gap, because the game currently has no word for it and prints 'you hold no office in this life yet' to somebody who just won.
whyItMatters: Winning is the payoff the whole campaign builds to, and in one of the two states measured the payoff is a sentence and then nothing, for months, on a screen that says the player has never run for anything. The owner has asked for lives carried past a first election into what follows; today, in Kentucky, nothing follows. Getting this right is also what makes multi-generation and long-life play coherent, because a term that starts on a date is the first thing in this game that puts a player's own future on the calendar.
